h2: NDT training options around Denver compared: college courses, on-the-job routes and online study with a hands-on practical
html:
NDT training options around Denver compared: college courses, on-the-job routes and online study with a hands-on practical

Search "NDT training near me" from Denver and you will find very little dedicated NDT schooling on the Front Range. In our review of public college catalogues for this page, we did not find a full NDT certificate or degree inside the Denver metro. What a Denver candidate can actually choose from is a welding-programme introduction, an out-of-state college programme, on-the-job training with an inspection company, a union route for oil and gas, or online theory paired with a hands-on practical at an employer. Here is what each gives you.

Who offers NDT training around Denver?

  • Welding programmes with an NDT introduction. Pikes Peak State College in Colorado Springs lists a four-credit welding course, WEL 1005, that introduces six NDT methods and concentrates on recognising weld discontinuities by eye against a welding code. It is a sound first look for a welder. It is not method-level UT, MT or PT training.
  • Kansas college programmes. The nearest full NDT programmes we verified are in Kansas: WSU Tech in Wichita, and Cowley College, whose NDT degree is available fully online through Cowley Online. A degree covers several methods plus general education, so it takes far longer than a single method course.
  • On-the-job training. Metro inspection companies hire assistants and trainees who learn beside certified staff. A 2026 Applied Technical Services listing for its Englewood office had trainees preparing equipment, supporting Level II technicians and documenting their training as assigned.
  • A union route for oil and gas. IUOE Local 112, an Operating Engineers local, describes training NDT personnel and placing them with oil and gas contractors throughout the country. That matters if DJ Basin pipeline work is your target.
  • Networking. A Colorado Section appears in ASNT's section meeting listings. Its meetings are where candidates meet working Level IIIs and the people who hire.

What Front Range employers ask for

Denver postings are specific. A 2025 listing for three NDE technician positions in the Denver area asked for Level II in UT thickness, MT and PT, at least three years of documented training, experience and certification, and eligibility for the company's vehicle insurance. The ATS Englewood listing wanted Level II in VT and MT for its technicians, plus a drug screen, a clean driving record and US person status under export rules. The pattern is consistent: a multi-method Level II in the surface methods plus UT thickness opens most field roles, and the hours must be on paper.

Looking for "destructive test training"? Destructive testing breaks a sample on purpose: bend, tensile and impact tests. It is taught in welding and materials-lab programmes, usually alongside welder qualification. NDT examines the part without damaging it, and NDT is all Atlantis teaches.

How to choose a Denver NDT training route

  • Hours. Do the training hours meet SNT-TC-1A's recommendation for your method and level, and does the record list topics and hours? Check your target with the SNT-TC-1A hours planner.
  • Certification. No school or course certifies you. Your employer does, under its written practice; ASNT certifies only after its own central exams.
  • Hands-on time. How many hours will you spend on real instruments and flawed specimens before the practical exam?
  • Level III access. Who answers technical questions while you train, and who writes and grades the exams?
  • Distance. Employers sit anywhere from Fort Collins to Colorado Springs. A programme that takes you off shift for weeks costs real income.

Where the Atlantis route fits for Denver candidates

There is no Atlantis classroom on the Front Range. You read the method theory online on your own timetable and put technical questions to an ASNT NDT Level III; access begins on the day you enrol. Set-up and scanning get rehearsed in the Practical NDT simulator. After that, your employer's own instruments and specimens are used for the hands-on practical and the practical exam, run under its SNT-TC-1A-based written practice, and the certification is issued by your employer, not by Atlantis. Start with NDT Level 1 training or, if you already hold Level I, NDT Level 2 training; the methods Denver postings ask for most are UT, MT and PT.

This route suits a technician who already works for an inspection company or plant, or who has a job offer. If you have no NDT employer yet and want lab hours before your first job, a college programme gives you that, and the online theory can sit alongside it. Employers building a certification programme for a whole crew can start with SNT-TC-1A training programme set-up. Check where you stand first with the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker.
